one_type_trace.name: Router
flow: Router::into_make_service and axum::serve consume the completed Router<()> service.

naming.files: Rust modules and source files use snake_case names (for example routing/method_routing.rs and serve/listener.rs); module roots use mod.rs.
naming.functions: Rust functions and tests use snake_case (for example into_make_service_with_connect_info and test_serve_local_addr); public APIs carry rustdoc comments.
naming.commits: CONTRIBUTING.md recommends a short first commit line, blank second line, and 72-column wrapping.

logging.pattern: Use tracing::trace!/error! for server lifecycle, connection, and protocol diagnostics; tests capture tracing subscribers when asserting events.

pitfalls.what: Router::merge panics when both routers have a custom fallback; Router::nest also panics for an empty or root path.
pitfalls.consequence: Dynamic or library-composed route construction can terminate the host process at startup instead of returning a recoverable error.

pitfalls.what: PathRouter route-layer and path composition enforce builder invariants through panic paths.
pitfalls.consequence: Middleware or route changes that violate ordering or path-conflict rules fail during construction and require matching should_panic/regression tests.

pitfalls.what: Multipart extraction is body-limit and header-format sensitive, with dedicated rejection behavior.
pitfalls.consequence: Changes to upload parsing can alter 413/error behavior and should be treated as a security-sensitive compatibility surface.

spec_compliance_evidence: CI runs strict rustdoc for axum-core, axum, and axum-extra.
CI tests stable and beta, axum-macros on its pinned nightly, and Rust 1.80 MSRV.
CI checks root and examples workspaces independently.

mandatory: add or extend a regression test under the affected crate
add unit/integration tests and strict rustdoc when public API changes

damage_control_rules: Never write or expose credentials from zero-access paths.
Learning writes are confined to the Agentify allowlist; application source, dependencies, workflows, policies, and runtime state require approval.

D1_topography.evidence_summary: Root inventory, README, and workspace manifest establish a Rust workspace centered on axum with library source under axum/src, examples, tests, CI, and contribution metadata.

evidence.excerpt: `axum` is an HTTP routing and request-handling library that focuses on ergonomics and modularity.

D2_module_boundaries.evidence_summary: axum/src separates routing, handler, extractor, response, middleware, and runtime transport layers with explicit imports and a Router-to-serve process boundary.

D3_type_contract.evidence_summary: Router is a documented public Rust contract with a generic missing-state parameter and Arc-backed inner routing state; the definition and service/state consumers are tracked in axum/src.

evidence.excerpt: Thus, only `Router<()>` (i.e. without missing state) can be passed to [`serve`].

D4_conventions.evidence_summary: Rust code uses snake_case module/file and function names, public APIs are documented inline, tests use descriptive test_* names and #[should_panic], and runtime diagnostics use tracing macros.

evidence.excerpt: #[should_panic(expected = "Nesting at the root is no longer supported. Use merge instead.")]
trace!("received graceful shutdown signal. Telling tasks to shutdown");

D5_pitfalls.evidence_summary: Routing composition has intentional panic-based invariants that can terminate an application during router construction, and the changelog records routing behavior as actively changing.

evidence.excerpt: panic!("Cannot merge two `Router`s that both have a fallback")
#[should_panic(expected = "Nesting at the root is no longer supported. Use merge instead.")]
Nesting at the root is no longer supported. Use `merge` instead.

D6_validation.evidence_summary: CI.yml defines locked workspace tests, clippy with warnings denied, rustfmt checks, strict docs, feature-matrix checks, MSRV/nightly tests, dependency/license checks, and cross-target checks; CONTRIBUTING.md requires tests for code changes.

evidence.excerpt: In both of these cases, the pull request should include one or more tests to ensure that the crate does not regress in the future.

D7_operational.evidence_summary: This is a Rust library workspace; Cargo is the build/package entry point, examples demonstrate runtime serving on localhost:3000, and release-plz publishes through main/v0.8.x workflows only for tokio-rs.

D8_security.evidence_summary: The workspace forbids unsafe Rust, and the existing Agentify policy protects runtime/policy/workflow state from learning writes; repository ignore rules do not cover common secret filenames, so those paths must remain zero-access in audit operations.

evidence.excerpt: Only .agentify agents, knowledge, history, manifest, and canonical ignore rules may self-update; policies, application source, dependencies, workflows, runtime code, and operational state are immutable to learning.

D9_process.evidence_summary: CONTRIBUTING.md documents issue discussion, triage, pull-request resolution and review, while GitHub issue templates identify bug and feature requests and CI.yml supplies repository validation gates.

evidence.excerpt: In the majority of cases, issues are resolved by opening a Pull Request.
Any Tokio, Hyperium, and Tower, axum community member is welcome to review any pull request.

D10_documentation.evidence_summary: README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, crate rustdoc, and CHANGELOG.md are the repository documentation surfaces; Agentify-generated files are not treated as application documentation.

evidence.excerpt: This guide will help you get started.

open_questions: No distinct agentic layer is part of the repository application architecture; .agentify-generated identities are excluded from process and documentation evidence.

exploration_log.observation: Created an honest gap-marked map to receive incremental audit evidence.

concerns.one_line: Owns public Router and MethodRouter composition, path matching, fallbacks, and conversion into tower services.
concerns.covers: Path syntax, method dispatch, nesting, merging, fallbacks, layers, state binding, URL parameters, HTTP method response rules, and routing tests/docs.
concerns.excludes: Handler extraction implementation, middleware authoring, hyper transport, and application response/body implementations.

flows.name: Request dispatch
flows.description: A request is matched, method-dispatched, and finalized as a response.

steps.what_happens: Router delegates request handling and fallback selection.
PathRouter matches the URI and dispatches the endpoint.
MethodRouter selects the method endpoint and builds 405 Allow behavior.

touchpoints.role: Public route composition, fallback state, and service conversion.
Matchit-backed path matching, validation, nesting, and merging.

invariants.rule: Overlapping methods and conflicting custom fallbacks panic during construction.
invariants.why: Method and fallback ownership must be unambiguous.

invariants.rule: Root nesting is forbidden; use merge or fallback_service.
invariants.why: The route tree has distinct root and fallback semantics.

invariants.rule: GET handles HEAD unless an explicit HEAD endpoint takes precedence.
invariants.why: This is the HTTP method contract.

pitfalls.risk: Using route_layer before routes or expecting it to affect unmatched requests.
pitfalls.consequence: Construction panics or the layer is skipped for 404s.

entry_questions: Does the change alter path syntax, overlap, fallback inheritance, nesting, or merge behavior?
Does it preserve Router<S> versus Router<()> service-state semantics?

concerns.concern: Request extraction, rejection, and body parsing
concerns.one_line: Owns conversion of requests into typed extractor values while enforcing ordering, content types, body limits, and typed rejections.
concerns.covers: FromRequest/FromRequestParts, request helpers, state references, body and form/JSON/multipart/path/query extraction, DefaultBodyLimit, rejection taxonomy, and docs/tests.
concerns.excludes: Routing production, tower middleware composition, full body framing, WebSocket upgrade mechanics, and general error-handling layers.

flows.name: Bounded typed extraction
flows.description: Parts extractors run first, the final body extractor consumes a limited body, and failures become typed responses.

steps.what_happens: Generated handlers execute parts extractors before the final body extractor.
The extract module exposes the core extractor contracts and feature-gated extractors, and provides shared content-type recognition.
with_limited_body applies configured or default body limits before collection.
Body, content-type, and deserialization failures map to composite rejection responses.

touchpoints.role: Core extractor contracts and blanket composition.

touchpoints.symbol: extract module exports, has_content_type, and consume_body test
touchpoints.role: Public extractor surface, feature-gated extractor composition, shared content-type check, and body-consumption regression coverage.

touchpoints.symbol: IntoResponse reexports and typed response helpers
touchpoints.role: Shared response contract used when extraction failures and extractor outputs become responses.

invariants.rule: Only the final handler extractor may consume the request body.
invariants.why: The body is a one-shot stream.

invariants.rule: Body collection uses DefaultBodyLimit or an explicit limit.
invariants.why: Body size is a security and compatibility boundary.

invariants.rule: Json requires application/json or an application +json subtype.
invariants.why: Unsupported content types reject before parsing.

pitfalls.risk: A custom extractor reads the body without with_limited_body.
pitfalls.consequence: The configured/default body limit may be bypassed.

entry_questions: Does the extractor consume the body, and is it last?
What content types, status codes, optional semantics, and body limits must remain stable?
validation: cargo test -p axum extract::json::tests extract::form::tests extract::multipart::tests

concerns.one_line: Owns axum::serve listener acceptance, hyper/tokio connection tasks, listener adapters, and signal-driven graceful draining.
concerns.covers: Serve futures, accept retry, hyper-util adaptation, Tokio executor, IncomingStream/connect-info, connection limits, IO hooks, and shutdown examples/tests.
concerns.excludes: Routing, handlers, middleware, application timeouts, and TLS/QUIC runtimes outside axum::serve.

flows.name: Serve and graceful drain
flows.description: The listener accepts connections, hyper serves them, and a signal drains in-flight tasks.

steps.what_happens: Serve::run accepts listeners and spawns hyper connection tasks.
Listener implementations retry transient accept failures and provide adapters.
The example supplies Ctrl-C/SIGTERM to with_graceful_shutdown.

touchpoints.role: Listener abstraction, retry, connection limits, and IO hooks.
Pins shutdown, timeout, executor, and IO behavior.

invariants.rule: Serve without graceful shutdown is unending; graceful shutdown waits for connection tasks to drain.
invariants.why: The accept loop and close channel define lifecycle completion.

invariants.rule: Transient accept errors are logged and retried.
invariants.why: Availability must survive transient listener failures.

invariants.rule: Accepted IO and address types satisfy async, Send/static, and diagnostic bounds.
invariants.why: hyper/tokio adapters and tasks require them.

pitfalls.risk: Graceful shutdown is used without bounding in-flight handlers.

entry_questions: Does the change affect accept retry, task spawning, or shutdown drain?
Can all in-flight work terminate before shutdown resolves?

concerns.one_line: Owns async-fn middleware, extractor gates, request/response mappers, and conversion of fallible tower services into axum responses.
concerns.covers: from_fn, from_extractor, map_request, map_response, Next, ResponseAxumBody, HandleError, Extension layers, Router/MethodRouter attachment, ordering, response composition, docs, and tests.
concerns.excludes: Routing tree composition, extractor implementation, hyper transport, body framing, and procedural macro plumbing.

flows.name: Middleware request and error path
flows.description: Middleware extracts/transforms a request, delegates to an inner service, and normalizes output or errors to Response.

steps.what_happens: FromFnLayer runs extractors and invokes user middleware with Next.
HandleError maps inner service errors through a user handler and IntoResponse.
The response module exposes IntoResponse, Response, Html, and NoContent composition used to materialize normalized middleware and error outputs.

touchpoints.role: Core public response contract and concrete response composition for middleware output and handled errors.

invariants.rule: Public middleware converts rejections/errors to Response and is generally Infallible.
invariants.why: Tower/hyper composition cannot leave failures as unhandled service errors.

invariants.rule: Fallible layers require HandleErrorLayer or ServiceExt::handle_error before Router attachment.
invariants.why: Router layer bounds require infallible-compatible errors.

invariants.rule: Router::layer runs after routing while route_layer applies only to matched routes.
invariants.why: Attachment position determines scope and rewrite behavior.

pitfalls.risk: Consuming the body in middleware without reconstructing it.
pitfalls.consequence: Downstream handlers/extractors see an empty body.

entry_questions: Does middleware need state, body access, short-circuiting, or response transformation?
Is the inner service fallible, and where should HandleError attach?

not_concerns.candidate: src, axum/src, or examples as directory names
not_concerns.why_rejected: Directories are not specialties; the retained concerns cross those boundaries.
No client or frontend source subtree was observed; axum/src is a server-side Rust library.
No repository-wide database or authentication flow exists in the core library; example-specific dependencies are not a core specialty.
The axum-macros tracer timed out, so no unsupported macro concern claims are recorded; future audit may trace it.

This tracked workflow orchestrates repository-wide Cargo formatting, lint, documentation, dependency, target, and test gates; it does not own routing, extraction, middleware, response, or server-transport behavior, which are recorded under validation_surface rather than a runtime specialty.
This tracked document defines repository-wide issue, pull-request, review, testing, and commit practices; it is lifecycle evidence rather than an end-to-end runtime behavior specialty.
